target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Boot-echo guard chunking used `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units and can split surrogate pairs (emoji, CJK beyond BMP, etc.), producing malformed chunks. This caused the substantial-echo comparison to miss matches when the alignment boundary falls inside a surrogate pair. Replace `.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` to preserve surrogate pair integrity during chunk extraction.

What changed: `getBootPromptChunks` and `containsSubstantialBootEcho` now use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from normalization-core instead of `String.prototype.slice()`. What did NOT change: algorithm, chunking logic, cache structure, public API, or behavior for ASCII/BMP-only text.

Fixes #110641

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The boot-echo guard fails to detect echoes when the boot prompt or outbound text contains characters outside the BMP (surrogate pairs), because `String.prototype.slice()` can split a surrogate pair and produce an invalid UTF-16 string that won't match the corresponding chunk.

**Root Cause**: In `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.ts`, both `getBootPromptChunks()` and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` used `.slice()` to extract comparison substrings. `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, the resulting string is malformed.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. A helper `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen()` wraps the safe slice to maintain the minimum chunk length invariant.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 6 boot-echo guard tests pass on current HEAD.

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

## Tests and validation

All 6 existing unit tests pass, confirming the UTF-16 safe chunking doesn't regress ASCII/BMP behavior.

## Risk checklist

- [X] This change is backwards compatible
- [X] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [X] Only changes internals of two functions; public API unchanged
